Audio / ESP32 / reverse engineering

Active Speakers ESP32 Controller

A volume/input controller for Hypex-based active speakers, built around the awkward fact that a good audio system is still a system: analogue levels, digital transport, balanced outputs, input selection, mute state and a USB protocol that was not designed to be charming.

Signal chain

The useful version of the diagram.

Vinyl through preamp and miniDSP, out over Toslink to a Topping DX5 II, then balanced XLR into the Hypex modules. The same setup also made RCA versus XLR, fixed versus variable output, and 96 kHz versus 192 kHz less abstract than they sound on spec sheets.

Debugging

When silence is still a signal.

The Hypex side has its own input, mute and volume state, separate from whatever the DAC is showing. Debugging it meant working down the chain rather than guessing: prove the Topping has signal, test RCA against XLR, check the Hypex input selection, then measure or trace what is actually coming out.

Controller

The ESP32 bit.

The controller work came from reverse-engineering the Hypex USB protocol with Wireshark, then building something physical to drive volume and source selection. It sits somewhere between hi-fi, embedded systems, and the special kind of stubbornness caused by wanting a proper knob.

Active Speakers ESP32 Controller Hypex, miniDSP, Topping, XLR and a proper knob.
